card.statement:
[(a)]
Let $(M,N)$ be a pair of commuting nilpotent matrices over a field $\mathbb F$, whose common null space <<ref:hbb>> is one-dimensional. Let <<ref:als0>> be the Weyr canonical form of $M$.
Then $(M,N)$ is similar to a pair of the form

\begin{equation}
\setlength{\arraycolsep}{2pt}
(W,B):=\left(\mat{0_{r_1}
&\left[\begin{smallmatrix}I\\0
\end{smallmatrix}\right]
&&0\\
&0_{r_2}
&\ddots&
\&&\ddots&\left[\begin{smallmatrix}I\\0
\end{smallmatrix}\right]
\\0&&&
0_{r_{k}}
},
\mat{J_{{r_1}}(0)
&\un B_{12}
&\dots&
\un B_{1k}\\
&J_{{r_2}}(0)
&\ddots&\vdots
\&&\ddots&\un B_{k-1,k}
\\0&&&
J_{r_k}(0)
}
\right)
\end{equation}

such that

- its first matrix $W$ is the Weyr canonical form of $M$,

- each $\un B_{1j}$ has the staircase form

\[
\left[\begin{MAT}(c){ccccccc}
&&&&&&0
\\\phantom{A} &&&&&&
\\ \text{\raisebox{-6pt}{$0$}}&&&&\ddots&&\\ &&&&&&
\addpath{(0,3,3)rr}
\addpath{(2,2,3)rr}
\addpath{(5,1,3)rr}\\
\end{MAT}\,\right]\]

whose stairs are located as the stairs of $\un S_{1j}$ in <<ref:rvt>>, and all nonzero entries of $\un B_{1j}$ are located on the stairs,

- each $\un B_{1+l,j+l}$ with $l\ge 1$
is a submatrix of
$\un B_{1j}$
that is located in its upper left corner.

- [(b)] In particular, if the Jordan canonical form of $M$ is

\begin{equation*}
J:=J_{k}(0)\oplus\dots\oplus J_{k}(0)\qquad (r\text{ summands}),
\end{equation*}

then $(M,N)$ is similar to a pair of the form

\begin{equation}
\setlength{\arraycolsep}{2pt}
(W,B):=\left(\mat{0_r&I_r&&&0_r\\
&0_r&I_r\\
&&0_r&\ddots\&&&\ddots&I_r\\0_r&&&&0_r},
\mat{J_r(0)&B_1&B_2&\ddots&B_{k-1}\\
&J_r(0)&B_1&\ddots&\ddots\\
&&J_r(0)&\ddots&B_2\\
&&&\ddots&B_1\\
0_r&&&&J_r(0)
}
\right)
\end{equation}

in which every $B_i$ is a matrix whose last row is arbitrary and the other rows are zero.
If the characteristic of\/ $\mathbb F$ is zero, then the pair <<ref:b6s0>> is uniquely determined by $(M,N)$.
card.label: Theorem 1

paper.title: Pairs of commuting nilpotent operators with one-dimensional intersection of kernels and matrices commuting with a Weyr matrix
paper.abstract: I.M. Gelfand and V.A. Ponomarev (1969) proved that the problem of classifying pairs (A,B) of commuting nilpotent operators on a vector space contains the problem of classifying an arbitrary t-tuple of linear operators. Moreover, it contains the problem of classifying representations of an arbitrary quiver, and so it is considered as hopeless. We give a simple normal form of the matrices of (A,B) if the intersection of kernels of A and B is one-dimensional. We prove that this form is canonical if the Jordan matrix of A is a direct sum of Jordan blocks of the same size and the field is of zero characteristic.
